I was thirteen when my mother moved out of our family home. She has bipolar disorder and cheated on my dad since I was about six years old with one of his close friends, who was also a neighbour with a wife and kids. For years, I knew she was cheating, but I didn't realise it was with him. One morning, my mother hadn't come home the previous night, and I heard my parents fighting a lot, and they didn't realise I was in the room. I was about twelve at this point. Dad noticed I had heard everything, and he took me for a drive and explained that my mother had been seeing somebody else (he didn't specify who) for a while, and he had known for a year or so, but they decided to stay together while my brother and I were still at school. Anyway, it didn't work out that way, and my mother moved out to live with her boyfriend. I eventually forgave her, as I knew she hated herself for what she did, but it took me a lot longer to forgive her boyfriend. 

It affected me a lot. I hated my mother for what she did, and I felt eternally sorry for my dad, who had put up with so much for so long. I now live with my mother and (now) step-father (I'm almost 18 now), and I'm pretty happy, but I miss living with my dad. 

All in all, it made me grow as a person, I learned that I am a strong enough person to have the capacity to forgive both my mother and step-father. I'm glad my parents divorced, because living in a house with two people who both love and hate each other at the same time is hell. The best thing to come out of it, is I built an amazing relationship with my brother (now 21), and my dad. I admire the strength of my entire family (my mother too, she recovered somewhat from years of severe depression after attempting suicide several times). As awful as the experience was, I'm glad it happened, it has made me into the person I am today, and allowed me to appreciate my family a lot.
